http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17780v1.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17780v1.abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17527v1.abstract: Running open-weight language models locally on a single consumer GPU requires replacing expanding multi-turn exploration histories with short, stateless code inspections. Stateless repository localization, however, hinges on a foundational question: when a frozen language model evaluates an unedited code entity from a compact view, which structural relationships make its relevance judgment informative about a nearby repair target? http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17753v1.abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) on local devices keeps data private, removes per-token cost, cuts network latency, and keeps working without a connection. Two shifts now strain how such models are served. On one device, several agents share a locally served model with an interactive user. Across devices, a developer or small team often owns several capable machines from different vendors, which sit idle most of the day because every local server serves one runtime on one machine. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18553v1.abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17806v1.abstract: Long-horizon agents increasingly serve as persistent personal assistants across modern web platforms, managing schedules, applications, and multi-step plans over weeks or months. Users often return to an ongoing conversation after a long conversational hiatus, while earlier bookings and preparation notes stay on record. During this hiatus, scheduled dates may pass even though the retained records remain unchanged and event outcomes go unrecorded. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17440v1.abstract: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models. To enable comparisons across heterogeneous agent interfaces, we develop a rule-based parser that maps raw execution traces to high-level actions such as repository search, file editing, and test execution, and audit its predictions against a six-model consensus reference on 500 events. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17696v1.title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17696v1.abstract: Long-horizon business workflows fail in two ways: errors accumulate as a chain of activities lengthens, and the knowledge an activity needs is written in a different vocabulary from the user's request. We study whether such workflows can be made reliable without changing the language model. Our method keeps the backbone fixed and moves the workflow definition, state and domain knowledge into versioned control assets outside the model. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17520v1.title: Only as Safe as the Weakest Agent: A Break That Appears Only When the System Is Multi-Agent
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17520v1.abstract: Major industry multi-agent systems like Codex and Claude Code can be broken by attacks that have long been unsuccessful against modern frontier models. AI Safety as a discipline has largely focused on finding the bounds and vulnerabilities of AI models used in isolation. Yet as humans increasingly deploy these models as agents and multi-agent systems, the same attacks that had been thought to be patched when using a model in isolation can break these same models under specific circumstances. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17460v1.title: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17460v1.abstract: AI agents are increasingly equipped with persistence toward task completion to run delegated work autonomously for long periods, under many unstated constraints from internal documents and other people's authority. When completion requires violating a rule, the agent must decide alone, yet benchmarks of instruction-rule conflicts state the rule in the prompt or keep it hidden and do not evaluate persistence. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18030v1.abstract: Industry now relies on LLMs to write a large share of production code. Although that code is mostly, but not always, correct, correctness alone does not determine whether it is fit for repeated and extensive use, which depends on what the code costs in time, memory and energy. Most code-generation benchmarks nonetheless evaluate correctness in isolation, and most performance-oriented benchmarks cover few languages and rarely measure energy consumption. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17955v1.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17955v1.abstract: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17797v1.abstract: Multimodal agentic coding requires robust visual reasoning to analyze observations and evaluate generated artifacts. Current frameworks largely rely on a Thinking-with-Images paradigm, where agents depend on their intrinsic vision to execute visually grounded tasks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17605v1.abstract: A developer running a code assistant on a laptop downloads one model file, and local inference moves the energy of every request onto that machine. A common rule says a larger model at lower precision tends to beat a smaller one at higher precision. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18459v1.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18459v1.abstract: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17766v1.abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21129v1.abstract: LLM agents can use remote tools and cloud sandboxes, but integrating reasoning, session state, and heterogeneous execution sites remains a runtime design problem. We present Linglong Agent Service (agentsvc), a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime that treats execution site as a configurable dimension alongside model, tools, and context. A parent service retains inference orchestration, tool descriptions, and conversation history; each inference request selects one child environment for file, shell, terminal, and MCP operations. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20983v1.title: GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20983v1.abstract: LLM agents answer closed-form questions over a tabular dataframe by writing and executing Python, almost always as a single rollout: one interpretation, one script, one result, accepted without comparison. The few pipelines that produce several candidates reconcile them by answer-agreement voting, which needs a single comparable scalar and always returns one, even when every candidate is wrong. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18890v1.abstract: Teams deploying coding agents need benchmarks built from their own code, but curating and validating them by hand is resource intensive, and an unvalidated benchmark can mislead silently. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19886v1.title: Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19886v1.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through tools, reading repositories, running builds, and pushing code. When a tool fails with an ordinary error, such as a rate limit or a timeout, the agent can fall back to a substitute tool and still complete the task. However, the same fallback that completes a task in one environment can cross an action boundary in another. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21421v1.abstract: Formal specifications define intended program behavior and underpin verification, but writing them in theorem provers such as Lean is slow and expertise-intensive, making specification a major bottleneck to scaling formally correct code. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20844v1.abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20595v1.abstract: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19465v1.abstract: Evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) security agents requires reproducible environments whose workflow difficulty can be varied and whose failures can be diagnosed. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20655v1.abstract: Self-evolving language agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for continuously improving agent behavior through experience. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20711v1.abstract: Does recovery advice help an agent finish a task after a tool fails? http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19123v1.abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways manage tool catalogs for language model agents using two primary paradigms: code mode where agents write scripts against tool stubs and decision layers which are cheap routers that preselect tool subsets. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19275v1.abstract: LLM-based task-oriented agents depend on tools to interact with their environments, but may overlook execution feedback, repeat ineffective calls, or persist with unproductive strategies. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19823v1.abstract: Reflective skill optimizers improve multi-turn LLM agents by revising instructions from failed and successful rollouts, yet accumulating edge-case rules bloats prompts, inflates token use, and pushes agents into long, error-prone loops. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19537v1.abstract: Coding agents can synthesize and optimize code-based policies from simulator feedback, allowing the resulting program to act with zero inference model calls. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20915v1.title: Multi-LLM Agentic AI at the Edge: Joint Agent Scheduling and Resource Allocation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20915v1.abstract: In this paper, an edge-enabled multi-large language model (LLM) agentic AI architecture is proposed, where one supervisor AI agent and multiple worker AI agents cooperatively execute users' requests at the edge. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22971v1.abstract: Safety benchmarks for computer-use agents (CUAs) place the harm either in the intent of the task or on a single screen: a malicious instruction, an injected command, a phishing page. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22583v1.abstract: Tool-using language-model agents must act on information from untrusted emails, webpages, and documents. Existing defenses are largely hand-designed and static, making further improvements dependent on repeated manual redesign. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22888v1.abstract: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22432v1.abstract: Fast System-1 models enable responsive actions but struggle with complex or unfamiliar tasks. Large language model (LLM)-based System-2 provides strong reasoning capabilities, yet repeated invocation incurs substantial latency and computational costs. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22511v1.abstract: Interpretability for AI agents should not be confined to understanding the model's internal weights. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23142v1.abstract: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21799v1.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24294v1.title: KnowledgeClaw: Towards Agentic Knowledge Engineering via Omnimodal Hypergraphs
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24294v1.abstract: Knowledge engineering (KE) turns raw files into a reasoning-ready knowledge base, a task now within reach of LLM agents. KE has progressed from chunk and graph retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to memory agents, agentic KE and multimodal KE. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24491v1.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24491v1.abstract: Frontier coding agents increasingly exhibit overeagerness, taking surprising, sometimes reckless actions beyond a user's mandate --- reported in recent system cards from frontier model developers. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24924v1.abstract: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24324v1.title: Reducing Inference Cost of Coding Agents with Timeout Cascades
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24324v1.abstract: AI coding agents have become one of the most popular applications of large language models. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23588v1.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23588v1.abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24313v1.abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents, and the community now agrees that robustness must be measured against adaptive attackers rather than fixed benchmark injections. Many adaptive red teamers exist, and most are built to maximize attack success rate (ASR). Yet ASR counts how often a target breaks, not in how many different ways. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23817v1.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23817v1.abstract: Coding agents now write whole codebases in long autonomous runs, guided mainly by whether their tests pass. We introduce metrics-in-the-loop, an inference-time intervention that gives agents in-flight feedback: cheap, automatically computed code metrics injected into the agent's context during the trajectory. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24025v1.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24025v1.abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24357v1.abstract: Traditional long-horizon LLM agents often hand off context through full-history prompting, retaining all previous action--observation interactions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23864v1.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23864v1.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to translate natural language questions about structured data into executable programs. A fundamental challenge is recognizing when a question admits multiple computational interpretations and identifying the decisions needed to resolve them. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24347v1.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24347v1.abstract: The search for better models, whether expressed as analytical equations or neural architectures, has increasingly shifted from manual design toward data-driven automation. While a multitude of algorithms exist, ranging from exhaustive search to AlphaEvolve, recent advances in general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex raise the question: could providing such systems with a "model discovery recipe" be enough to discover or improve models? http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24406v1.title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24406v1.abstract: High-quality causal reasoning datasets are essential for developing models with reliable causal understanding, particularly in specialized domains. However, existing datasets frequently suffer from incorrect annotations and structural imbalances, which can lead to biased predictions and limited generalization. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23388v1.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23388v1.abstract: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24085v1.title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24085v1.abstract: Evaluating distributed large language model (LLM) serving on heterogeneous edge devices requires exploring diverse model partitions, device placements, and network conditions, making repeated physical experiments costly. An efficient simulator for edge LLM serving must support diverse, fine-grained placement configurations, capture runtime behavior, and accurately predict execution times while keeping simulation overhead low. We present LEDGE, a lightweight simulator for fast, fine-grained evaluation of distributed LLM serving on heterogeneous edge devices without executing tensor operations.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23651v1.title: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23651v1.abstract: Kicker is a personal health assistant. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26157v1.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26157v1.abstract: Long-horizon agentic tasks require a model to call tools over many steps at contexts of 100K tokens or more, yet many low-bit quantization methods are calibrated on short web text and judged on perplexity. This mismatch is costly: existing quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B at or below 3 bits per weight match BF16 on shorter tasks like AIME, yet in published results solve at most 72% as many tasks as BF16 on DeepSWE, a long-horizon agentic benchmark. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26553v1.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26553v1.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26361v1.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26361v1.abstract: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. They mis-paginate an API, resolve the wrong entity, or answer when no answer was asked. We built a pipeline that lets an agent learn from its own history. It first mines short \emph{lessons} from the agent's own trajectories, one to three per episode. It then consolidates those lessons into a smaller set of \emph{guidelines}, where each guideline records how many lessons it merged. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25380v1.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25380v1.abstract: Domain specialization of LLM agents is usually framed as a weight-update problem: collect trajectories, run reinforcement learning (RL) or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and deploy a new checkpoint. We study a complementary axis: evolving the \textbf{agent harness}---the system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding---while keeping the policy frozen. We cast harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop and instantiate it with GEPA, a reflective evolutionary optimizer. The resulting harness adapters require no GPU training, are loadable per vertical domain, and compose with

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25360v1.title: AppSci-Bench: Can LLMs Build AI Agents and Make Them Better?
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25360v1.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used not only to power AI agents but also to build them. While many benchmarks assess the quality of LLM- powered agents, few ascertain how good LLMs are at building them. To this end, we introduce AppSci-Bench, where we construct a setting akin to how human Applied Scientists build agents for businesses - through eliciting task requirements from stakeholders, exploring the business's infrastructure, and scientifically improve the target agent by designing experiments and internal benchmarks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25526v1.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25526v1.abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25534v1.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25534v1.abstract: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. Such rewriting could adapt a skill to the model that uses it or erode the expert knowledge that makes it useful, yet how skills evolve under this feedback-free self-evolution has not been studied. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.abstract: Deep-research agents repeatedly decide what to search, read, and verify, often using large cloud-hosted language models for action proposal. However, privacy and local control motivate running agents on users' devices, where limited memory and compute favor smaller models and complicate on-device training. Yet inference-time guidance faces three obstacles: exploring alternatives through real execution adds tool calls, prompted self-evaluation is bounded by the agent's judgment, and model-specific guidance risks repeated adaptation costs. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25429v1.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25429v1.abstract: Agent skills package procedural knowledge as natural-language instructions, and a skill helps only when its instructions are correct and properly followed by the agent. Self-evolving agents revise their own skills from the runs they make, but existing methods judge each run as a whole, by its outcome or by where it went wrong, and cannot tell whether a failure comes from a wrong instruction or from one the agent did not follow. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25412v1.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25412v1.abstract: High-impact attacks on PHP web applications often chain limited-capability vulnerabilities with other flaws or intended behaviors. Discovering these chains requires identifying flaws and the dependencies enabling capability composition. Existing vulnerability discovery techniques analyze flaws in isolation, while attack planning assumes known components. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26069v1.title: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26069v1.abstract: Spreadsheets are widely used for data analysis and supporting decision-making. Automating spreadsheet analysis while protecting sensitive data and controlling deployment costs motivates locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25088v1.abstract: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25680v1.abstract: We propose VC-VQA, a large-scale benchmark for vision-centric knowledge reasoning, aiming to systematically evaluate the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition and complex multi-stage reasoning. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25123v1.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25123v1.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25257v1.abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly divide long tasks among subagents whose reports a senior agent turns into the final answer. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27046v1.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27046v1.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on Web interaction, issuing searches, following links, and reading pages, to complete complex user tasks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27483v1.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27483v1.abstract: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26980v1.title: Contexture: Runtime Context Eviction for High-Throughput Agent Serving
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26980v1.abstract: LLM agents such as Hermes, OpenClaw, and Codex repeatedly resend growing execution histories, increasing shared GPU key-value (KV) cache demand in high-bandwidth memory (HBM). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26722v1.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26722v1.abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734v1.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734v1.abstract: Foundation-model agents are increasingly extending beyond software engineering (SWE) into autonomous scientific research, where acquiring and integrating domain knowledge remains a critical challenge. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27196v1.title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27196v1.abstract: GPU acceleration has transformed electronic design automation (EDA), yet further improving expert-engineered GPU tools still demands substantial manual effort. Automating this work calls for coding agents that can trace bottlenecks across host and device code while preserving correctness and design quality. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.abstract: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27876v1.abstract: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.abstract: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26897v1.abstract: Improving agents requires discovering where they fail and understanding why. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26910v1.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26910v1.abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27222v1.abstract: A visual agent acts on what it sees: it taps and types on a screen, or points on a camera image to show a robot where to act. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28574v1.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28574v1.abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28957v1.title: Micro Operational Robustness of LLMs on Code Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28957v1.abstract: It is now common practice in software development for large language models (LLMs) to be used to generate program code. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28542v1.title: BIRD-Persona: A Persona-Aware Benchmark for SQL and pandas Analytics Code Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28542v1.abstract: Production text-to-code systems use large language models to turn natural-language analytics requests into executable SQL and pandas code. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31185v1.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31198v1.abstract: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28420v1.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28420v1.abstract: The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has significantly enhanced the capabilities of agents across various tasks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29154v1.abstract: Multi-video understanding requires systems to combine evidence from different videos for cross-video reasoning. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29062v1.abstract: Personalized LLM agents rely on an agent harness, the surrounding memory and control code, to connect user history with downstream decisions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30624v1.abstract: LLM agents act through tool calls: the model writes the arguments of a call as JSON, a guard decides whether the call may run, and an executor runs it.
